With a somewhat large family, the fridge takes a pounding, constantly being used and abused. I have been trying to make our fridge last just a little longer because it runs perfectly but our drawers and shelves were getting so "used" looking. One shelf started getting a crack in it and we actually duct taped it!! lol
So we've been living with an embarrassingly overused refrigerator with duct taped shelves and I would absolutely cringe when guests would come over and see the eyesore! then one day I saw replacement drawers and shelves and thought I would give it a shot. All I needed was the model number of the fridge and measured the existing shelf just to be sure. This shelf was so easy to slide into the door and I could finally throw out the ugly duct taped shelf! I plan to replace the drawers next. This saved us a whole lot of extra moola not having to replace our fridge quite yet. Yay!

When I need ice, I merely bounce the bag on the counter a couple of times to break-up the ice and it's ready for any size container.

So Far, So Good. I read a lot of the other reveiws and tried to avoid making mistakes. I let the machine rest for a day in it's new position before turing it on for the first time. I ran about 2 days worth of ice through it to get out the "plastic" taste, before getting usable good tasting ice.

It's now a favored appliance! Each batch seems small and non consequencial, but in about an hour's time, there's enough ice to stuff a lagre quart size ice tea glass full of ice. The mahine will refill and go to sleep before your ice tea is ready for a refill. We've started a bag of ice in the freezer, incase two of us needing ice at the same time. The ice is a bit "wet" and freezes togeteher, but a sharp rap of the ziplock bag on the counter solves that when about to fill your glass.

Be careful whe re-inserting the ice tray, as if it's off just a little bit, it will trigger the Ice Full sensor, and put the machine to sleep. The tray needs to be "front justified".

I like that I can make ice out of whatever brand of bottled water I'm using for the day. So if Drinking brand A, it's not diluted with ice from tap water or some filtered source not quite of the same taste.

We're finding that it's not entirely a waste to let the last batch of ice for the day melt back into the water tank. It keeps the water colder and leads to larger ice pellets, than if the machine starts with room temp water. Same for filling the machin
